A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated. Every stage I patient who is too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy (3-8 visits, no anaesthesia) instead of being left without treatment. The treatment exists in every university hospital; what is missing in some counties is the referral rule.
effect_summary_en: In the Netherlands, 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated once stereotactic radiotherapy was available. That supports the direction of the effect, but the share of all patients (0.8 points) comes from our own model, not from the study.
supported_en: A national Dutch registry study (Annals of Oncology, 2012) found 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated once stereotactic radiotherapy was fully available.
not_supported_en: The pages do not show how much the share of all patients treated with intent to cure would rise in Finland (our model assumes 0.8 points).
in_use_quote: Jos leikkaus ole mahdollinen, hoitomuoto voi olla korkea-annoksinen niin sanottu täsmäsädehoito osassa tapauksia.
missing_en: No page shows a rule that every stage I patient who is too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy.
summary_en: HUS's lung cancer care pathway page (updated 15.06.2026) says that when surgery is not possible, high-dose targeted radiotherapy may be used "in some cases". No page shows a rule that every frail stage I patient is referred. Kymenlaakso county's page says radiotherapy is given at Kymenlaakso Central Hospital in Kotka. A Dutch national registry study (2012) found 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated after stereotactic radiotherapy became available.
unanswered_en: I found no page saying whether Kymenlaakso Central Hospital itself gives stereotactic lung radiotherapy, and no page with a referral rule for frail stage I patients.
